entities.summary: Johann Georg of Hohenzollern-Hechingen was the first Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, a position he held from 1615 until his death in 1623. He was the son of Frederick of Hohenzollern-Hechingen and Dorothea of Anhalt-Ascherfeld. Born into a minor German noble family, Johann Georg's early life was marked by the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various German states. In 1615, he inherited the principality of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, a territory that had been a minor player in European politics for centuries. Despite his limited powers, Johann Georg played a key role in the Thirty Years' War, supporting the Protestant cause against the Catholic Habsburgs. He died on September 28, 1623, without an heir, leading to a succession crisis that would shape the fate of the Hohenzollern dynasty for centuries to come. Johann Georg's legacy can be seen in the many Hohenzollern princes who followed in his footsteps, including Frederick William, the first King of Prussia. Despite his relatively minor status, Johann Georg's actions had far-reaching consequences for the balance of power in Europe and the development of the Hohenzollern dynasty.
